column2: The call to all Israel recalls what they saw done to Pharaoh, his servants and his whole land, preserving all three objects.
Great trials, signs and great wonders remain the content of the eyewitness recollection.
The Lord God has not given the knowing heart, seeing eyes or hearing ears until this day; the negative is not softened into human inability alone.
Forty wilderness years are linked to garments not ageing and sandals not wearing away from the feet.
No bread, wine or strong drink leads to knowing that He is the Lord their God; the selected third-person wording is retained.
You came is followed by the kings meeting us and we smote them; the changes of person remain.
We took the land but I gave it, retaining Moses' role and the Reuben, Gad and half-Manasseh allocation.
Understanding all that they do preserves syniete rather than replacing it with prospering.
Tribal chiefs, elders, judges and recording officers precede every man of Israel in the gathering.
column3: Recording officers remains the working administrative rendering of grammatoeisagogeis; institutional precision is unresolved.

column2: Wives, children and the resident sojourner join the gathering, with woodcutter through water carrier preserving its stated range.
Entry includes both covenant and its curses, retaining arai rather than reducing the statement to an unspecified oath.
Being established as God's people and His being their God are linked to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob by name.
Not with you alone applies to both this covenant and this curse.
Those present and those absent are included, with here, with us and today deliberately repeated.
We dwelt and we passed lead to the final you passed; the person change is not harmonized.
Abominations and idols are described by wood, stone, silver and gold in that order.
Man, woman, family and tribe are all possible bearers of a turned mind; the root springs in gall and bitterness.
The self-blessing, wandering heart and explicit protection of the guiltless from the sinner remain; the final purpose clause is not omitted as awkward.
column3: Hosia moi genoito, the causal hoti rendered though, and the attachment of the final hina clause require fuller syntactic and lexical review. Inherited punctuation and May it be well with me are provisional.

column2: Emphatic refusal of mercy precedes anger, jealousy, all written covenant curses and the blotting out of the offender's name.
The Lord separates the offender for evils from all Israel according to the written curses, preserving the singular target.
The coming generation and distant foreigner see the land's plagues and diseases and introduce the subsequent question.
Sulfur, salt, burning and total absence of growth precede the four-city comparison: Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim.
All nations ask both why the land was treated thus and about the great heat of anger.
Abandonment of the fathers' covenant made at the exodus is the stated answer.
Service and worship of unknown gods not allotted to them remain distinct from the earlier covenantal relation.
Wrath against the land brings all curses written in this law book, not just a selected subset.
Removal and casting into another land retain wrath, anger and exceedingly great indignation, ending with the present comparison.
Hidden things belong to God, revealed things to us and our children for ever, with doing all the law as the purpose; retain the selected chapter boundary.
Blessing and curse received into the heart occur among the nations of dispersion, beginning the restoration condition.
Returning and obeying require all heart and all soul; no absent children clause is supplied here.
Healing sins preserves the selected Greek rather than substituting restoring fortunes or captivity; mercy and renewed gathering follow.
Both ends are ends of heaven, and from thence plus the full divine title is repeated for gathering and taking.
Return is to the fathers' inherited land, with good and numerical increase beyond the fathers retained.
Thoroughly cleanse represents perikathariei rather than importing circumcision; both the people's and their seed's hearts are in view.
The curses move to enemies and haters who pursued Israel, preserving the past persecution clause.
Return, hearing and doing the commanded precepts are retained as three linked actions.
Care greatly preserves the selected polyoresei; generic ktenon is revised from cattle to livestock, keeping womb, land and livestock order.
Commandments, ordinances and judgments are all named, and the second condition repeats whole-hearted and whole-souled return.
Neither excessive burden nor distance characterizes the command, preserving the two different descriptions.
The imagined ascent is into heaven above to fetch the command for hearing and doing.
The corresponding sea crossing includes making the command heard as well as fetching it, preserving the fuller parallel.
Mouth, heart and hands all remain in the selected nearness statement; hands is not removed to harmonize a familiar quotation.
The selected order is life and death, good and evil, rather than re-pairing life with good and death with evil.
The conditional obedience includes loving, walking in all ways and keeping ordinances and judgments, leading to life, numbers and blessing.
Turning of heart, non-hearing, being led astray, worship and service remain a sequence of departure.
Sure destruction and denial of long life retain their emphases before the Jordan-crossing inheritance description.
Heaven and earth witness life/death and blessing/curse; choosing life is for both the addressee and the seed.
This, not He, represents touto in the life statement; love, hearing and cleaving lead to dwelling in the land sworn to the three named patriarchs.
Moses finished speaking preserves the selected synetelesen, not a familiar alternative that he went.
Moses is 120 this day, with inability to go in and out and the prohibition on crossing this Jordan both retained.
The Lord Himself destroys the nations and Joshua goes before the people; the two agents are not conflated.
Sihon and Og are explicitly the two Amorite kings beyond Jordan, with their land included in the comparison.
The selected delivered is past tense, followed by future conduct as commanded; it is not harmonized to a future delivery.
Courage and strength precede three prohibitions on fear, faintheartedness and terror; divine presence and the two assurances remain.
Moses publicly addresses Joshua, with the oath to our fathers and Joshua's assigning the inheritance retained.
The Lord accompanies Joshua and will neither fail nor forsake him, followed by both prohibitions on fear and faintheartedness.
The law is written in a book and given to both the ark-bearing Levitical priests and the elders.
Seven years, the release year and the Feast of the Pitching of Tents specify the public-reading occasion.
All Israel appears at the chosen place, where the law is read before them in their hearing.
Men, women, children and resident sojourner gather to hear and learn fear, with hearing-to-do retained at the end.
Their sons who do not know are to hear and learn for all their days in the land beyond the Jordan.
Moses' approaching death prompts Joshua's summons; the doors of the Tent of Testimony are repeated in command and fulfilment.
The Lord descends in a cloud and stands at the doors, followed by the cloud pillar standing there; both clauses remain.
Moses' sleep with the fathers contrasts with the people's rising to pursue foreign gods, forsake God and break the covenant.
Plural them gives way to singular collective people/it and then the people's first-person confession, matching the source's shifts.
The emphatic turning away of the divine face answers the people's turning to foreign gods.
The song is written, taught and put in their mouth as a witness for God among Israel; the selected plural commands are not assigned exclusively to one actor.
The good milk-and-honey land leads to eating, filling and satiety before turning, serving, provoking and covenant-breaking.
The song stands as witness and is not forgotten by either their mouth or their seed's; present wickedness before entry is explicitly known.
Moses writes and teaches the song on that day, preserving both fulfilment actions.
Moses is the selected speaker to Joshua, and the Lord is referred to in the third person; neither is harmonized to an alternative speaker tradition.
Completion of all the law's words in a book unto the end introduces the custodial command.
The addressees are the Levites who bear the covenant ark, retaining the specific office.
The book is beside the ark, not inside it. Revise against you to among you for en soi, leaving its adversarial function to context rather than substituting a preposition.
Moses' knowledge of provocation and stiff neck while alive grounds the stronger expectation after death.
Tribal chiefs, elders, judges and recording officers hear the words, with heaven and earth invoked as witnesses.
Emphatic lawlessness after Moses' death leads to departure from the commanded way and later evils provoked by their handiwork.
Moses speaks the whole song to the whole assembly, retaining unto the end before the song begins.
